title: Philly Cheesesteak Egg Rolls
seoTitle: Philly Cheesesteak Egg Rolls | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Crunchy handhelds for watch night
description: Crunchy handhelds for watch night. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Cook and sauce filling
steps.instruction: Slow-cook or simmer filling until shreddable (pork 203°F, meatballs cooked through). Simmer in sauce 15 minutes so flavor penetrates.

steps.title: Toast buns
steps.instruction: Toast split buns on a dry griddle until golden. Melt cheese on top if desired.

steps.title: Build the sandwich line
steps.instruction: Philly Cheesesteak Egg Rolls on sheet trays: bottom bun, meat, sauce, cheese, top bun. Serve immediately; hold wrapped sandwiches at 200°F up to 20 minutes.

steps.title: Hold for late calls
steps.instruction: Keep backup sandwiches foil-wrapped at 200°F. Slice hoagies in half for easier grabbing — crew eats with one hand when tones are quiet.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Philly Cheesesteak Egg Rolls with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Build a long snack board: mains down the center, dips and chips at both ends.
Use disposable boats for handhelds so cleanup stays under five minutes after the game.
Line up Philly Cheesesteak Egg Rolls on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Crunchy handhelds for watch night. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
